thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 Alert: P99 latency spike detected for route 'api.v1.generate' in us-west-2. SLO p99 > 2.5s for last 5m. PagerDuty incident created (PD#INC-4129).

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident INC-4129 — High latency (P99) — Triggered. Auto-page to on-call.

sofia ramos: ack — I'm on it. grabbing metrics and tail logs.

nate yang: pinging in. can someone share which model/route? looks like heavy short-ctx gen.

sofia ramos: route = api.v1.generate, model = rdx-13b-1, traffic 85% PLG + burst from a single partner. no error rate increase, just tail latency.

jamal khan: checking infra: autoscaler is healthy, but GPU mem across pool inference-prod shows high fragmentation. KV-cache eviction rate spiked ~5m ago.

mira patel: adding: traces show repeated cold KV cache misses for the same prefixes — likely cache thrash from bursty multi-tenant keys. p95 increased slightly but p99 drove the page.

sofia ramos: quick mitigation options: 1) shift partner traffic to a fallback model (rdx-6b) 2) temporarily increase pool size by 2 GPUs 3) flush/rewarm KV cache for hot prefixes 4) enable per-tenant rate limit for the partner. Any objections?

nate yang: 1 & 2 are fastest. I'm in favor of shift -> fallback then scale if needed. shifting should be a config route change, low-risk.

jamal khan: I can scale now. running:

```bash
# scale inference-prod pool by +2 GPUs
rwctl capacity adjust --pool inference-prod --delta 2 --reason "p99 spike scaleup"
```

sofia ramos: doing traffic shift now to fallback model for partner token prefixes.

```yaml
# routing override (applied via Control Plane)
route: api.v1.generate
overrides:
  - match: tenant_prefix: "partner:acme-"
    model: rdx-6b-fallback
    weight: 1.0
```

sofia ramos: applied override; partner traffic now hits rdx-6b-fallback. monitoring...

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: INC-4129 acknowledged by sofia ramos. Escalation paused.

mira patel: initial effect: partner p99 dropped from ~4.2s -> ~1.8s within two minutes. overall cluster p99 improved from 3.1s -> 2.0s. good signal.

nate yang: scaling complete: +2 GPUs added to inference-prod, pods entering Ready. This should reduce KV eviction cadence and allow rewarm.

jamal khan: I also pushed a temporary KV cache TTL bump for hot prefixes to reduce churn:

```json
{"cache_prefix":"partner:acme-","ttl_seconds":300}
```

sofia ramos: customer impact: no errors observed, only increased latency for a small set of partner requests (10k qps at peak). No data loss. Notifying CS & product for partner outreach.

mira patel: running a quick sanity eval on generation quality for fallback model; outputs look acceptable for short prompts. noting in incident notes.

sofia ramos: plan: 1) keep fallback for partner for next 30m while capacity stabilizes 2) re-evaluate KV cache eviction patterns and adjust rewarm logic 3) follow up with partner about traffic smoothing 4) file a runbook update for similar tenant-driven thrash cases.

jamal khan: created infra task INFRA-789 to investigate fragmentation and a request to infra for pool isolation per top-tier partners.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: INC-4129 status updated — Mitigated. Auto-close scheduled in 30m if no regression.

sofia ramos: closing notes: mitigation effective, p99 returned under SLO for 10+ consecutive minutes. will hand off a short post-incident writeup. leaving paging open while we watch for 30m.

oncall-rotation: thanks team — great quick coordination. please add follow-up owners in the ticket. :thumbsup:

sofia ramos: will write the postmortem and include timeline + config diffs. assigning owners: jamal (infra follow-up), mira (model fallback eval), nate (scale/autoscaler safeties), me (postmortem & partner comms).

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: INC-4129 closed automatically after Mitigated state.

incident-bot: Incident log appended: INC-4129 — kv-cache thrash + partner burst => traffic shift + scale => mitigated.

sofia ramos: thanks all. follow-up kickoff in #eng-runtime tomorrow 10:00.
